name: Adriano Santos
action: Adriano sets down the screwdriver, picks up the phone, and answers in his usual too-loud voice: "Marina. I'm still on the drum. I can come for a while after I finish this lug, but I can't stay the whole time. Tell Mom I'll try."
reason: Adriano's first impulse was to give Marina a vague excuse and get back to the turquoise wrap, using the drum as a way to avoid the loud family lunch. Reflection softened that impulse: he recognized that a vague reply would leave her waiting, that he had already skipped three Sundays, and that his urge to hide in the garage echoed his father's old habit of slipping away when family life got heavy. Because he values honesty and dislikes lies, he could not bring himself to use the drum as an outright excuse. His revised tendency was to offer a qualified yes rather than a dodge, and he follows it by telling Marina he will come for a short while after finishing the wrap, without committing to the whole meal. The remaining conflict between his need to control his surroundings and his wish not to let Marina down is expressed in the hesitation and limits he puts on the promise, leaving room to leave early if the noise becomes too much.
